instructions.question: Does the poster of this Serbian tweet lean positive (warmth, fun, liking, cheering), lean negative (complaint, annoyance, mockery, sarcasm, sadness, self-put-down), or show no lean at all (neutral)?
instructions.rule: Mild feelings count: any gripe, sarcasm, mockery of people, politics or media, or joke about one's own failures is negative, even when it is funny or has a smiley. Any warmth counts as positive: laughter, greetings and shout-outs, cheering, compliments, wishes, or enjoying something. Use neutral only for plain information, plans, questions, quotes or aphorisms, and jokes with no gripe and no warmth. For headlines, follow the event: crime, death or scandal is negative; success, wins, new releases or promotions are positive; routine items are neutral.

neutral.what: Plain information, plans, questions, factual remarks, quotes and aphorisms without warmth or complaint, and routine news or announcements.
examples: Sednica SB UN o Kosovu 10. februara u Njujorku (UN SC session on Kosovo Feb 10 in New York)
Gledacu serije. (I'll watch series.)
RT @MakiJaffa: Dobri ljudi ti donose srecu. Losi iskustvo. (Good people bring you luck. Bad ones experience.)
neutral.cues: plain statements, jel (is it), danas (today), times and dates, link-only shares, neutral RTs of sayings
neutral.not_for: Anything with a gripe or mockery is negative. Anything with fun, warmth or cheering is positive.

positive.what: Tweets showing warmth, fun, liking, laughter, cheering, greetings, compliments, wishes or enjoyment, even if low-key or with swearing. Upbeat headlines and promotions.
examples: @pUnaVuna jel ti radis ili rtw-ujes :-) Elem, do jaja si :-) (are you working or retweeting :-) anyway, you're awesome)
Ajmoo Doktori @doktorixfactor #xfactoradria (Come on Doktori!)
Pozdrav za @atjah sa kruševačke obilaznice ;) (Greetings to @atjah from the Kruševac bypass ;))
Serena Vilijams teniserka godine (Serena Williams tennis player of the year)
positive.cues: HAHAHA, :) ;) :* <3 with friendly words, ajmo (come on), pozdrav (greetings), do jaja (awesome), car (king), volim (I love), uživam (I enjoy), srećan (happy)
positive.not_for: Sarcastic 'Volim kad...' (I love it when...) or mock praise is negative. Smileys on top of a complaint are negative.

negative.what: Complaints, mild gripes about daily life (school, waking up, Monday, boredom, internet), annoyance, sadness, insults, and sarcasm or mockery of people, couples, Facebook habits, politicians or media. Also self-deprecating jokes and headlines about crime or scandal.
examples: Mrzim ponedeljak (I hate Monday)
Moje pauze od ucenja traju duze nego samo ucenje (My study breaks last longer than the studying)
Volim kad obucem jaknu i onda mi kosa pozadi odjednom postaje gnezdo koje nikada nije ocesljano (I love it when I put on my jacket and my hair turns into a never-combed nest)
Srpski bokser ubijen zbog ucene (Serbian boxer killed over blackmail)
negative.cues: mrzim (I hate), najgore (the worst), jebi ga (damn), dosada (boredom), bljak (yuck), koji kurac (what the hell), stop, glup (stupid), :( , ironic 'naravno' (of course), ubijen/uhapšen (killed/arrested)
negative.not_for: Playful banter that is affectionate is positive. Factual political or news statements without mockery are neutral.
